newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: COLOMBIA SLAMS BRAZILIAN COFFEE QUOTA-BUSTING.
newsitem.headline: COLOMBIA SLAMS BRAZILIAN COFFEE QUOTA-BUSTING.

text.p: Colombia's private coffee exporters launched a bitter attack Wednesday on Brazil for its "flagrant violation" of export quotas.

The influential Association of Colombian Coffee Exporters (ASOEXPORT) said in its bi-monthly organ "Carta Cafetera" that Brazil overstepped its 15 million 60-kg bag quota for the period June 1996 to June this year by 8 percent or 1.2 million bags.

"Difficulties with complying with the provision of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries'(ACPC) quotas or their flagrant violation invite the parties to the agreements to evasion," ASOEXPORT wrote.
"When it comes to fulfilling promises and agreements, we don't know how many times our main partner Brazil will disappoint us," it added.
Tension between Colombian and Brazilian coffee growers is nothing new, but the tone of the attack by ASOEXPORT was one of the harshest to date.
At a recent event to celebrate the 70th anniversary of the creation of Colombia's National Coffee Growers' Federation, ACPC chief Rubens Barbosa confirmed Brazil had exceeded its pre-agreed quotas.

ASOEXPORT accused Brazil of taking advantage of soaring international prices earlier this year to sell as much coffee as it could to alleviate the deficit in the current account of its balance of payments.
